chapters.category: Hebrew, Greek, and Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 2 — Creation and the Holy Sabbath
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest primary-language witnesses responsibly available for this chapter. The Hasmonean Hebrew manuscript 4Q216 (4QJubileesᵃ), columns 5–7, governs every physically preserved reading throughout verses 1–24. Ancient Greek excerpts preserved by Epiphanius and Syncellus govern their extant portions of verses 2–4, 7, 11–13, 15, and 18–23. Physical gaps and the complete wording of all 33 verses follow the Ethiopic (Geʽez) text preserved in manuscripts A–D and printed on text pages 5–9 of R. H. Charles’s 1895 critical edition, The Ethiopic Version of the Hebrew Book of Jubilees. No modern English translation was used as the translation base, no commentary was used as Scripture, and no wording absent from these primary witnesses was supplied.

verses.text: The angel of the presence said to Moses according to the Lord’s word: ‘Write the complete account of creation—how in six days the Lord God finished all his works and everything he created, rested on the seventh day, sanctified it for all ages, and appointed it as a sign for all his works.
verses.study: The creation account is delivered as commanded testimony. The seventh day is not an afterthought but the enduring sign toward which the six days move.
crossReferences: Genesis 2:1–3 — God finishes his work, rests, blesses, and sanctifies the seventh day
Exodus 31:16–17 — the Sabbath is an enduring sign grounded in six-day creation

verses.text: On the first day he created the upper heavens, the earth, the waters, and all the spirits that serve before him: the angels of the presence, the angels of holiness, the angels of the spirits of fire and wind, the angels of the spirits of clouds, darkness, snow, hail, frost, dew, and rain, the angels of voices, thunder, and lightning, the angels of the spirits of cold and heat, winter, spring, autumn, and summer, and every spirit of his creatures in heaven and on earth. He also created the abysses and darkness, evening and night, light, dawn, and day, which he prepared by the knowledge of his heart.
verses.study: The first day displays a creation already ordered for divine service. Heavenly ministers, seasons, weather, darkness, and light all belong to the Creator’s knowledgeable design.
crossReferences: Psalm 104:2–4 — God clothes himself with light and makes winds and fire his ministers
Daniel 7:9–10 — innumerable heavenly servants attend the divine throne

verses.text: Then we saw his works, blessed him, and praised him before his presence because of all his works, for he made seven great works on the first day.
verses.study: The angels’ first response to creation is worship. Seeing the ordered works leads directly to blessing and praise of their maker.
crossReferences: Job 38:4–7 — heavenly beings rejoice when God establishes the earth
Psalm 148:1–5 — angels and heavenly hosts praise the Creator

verses.text: On the second day he made the expanse in the midst of the waters. The waters were divided on that day: half went up above, and half went down beneath the expanse that was in the midst over the face of the whole earth. This was the one work he made on the second day.
verses.study: The expanse orders the primal waters into upper and lower regions. Creation advances through separation that makes an inhabited world possible.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:6–8 — the expanse divides waters above from waters below
Psalm 148:4 — waters above the heavens join creation’s praise

verses.text: On the third day he commanded the waters to withdraw from the face of the whole earth into one place so that dry land might appear.
verses.study: God’s command establishes the boundary between sea and land. The habitable earth appears through obedience to his word.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:9 — gathered waters allow dry land to appear
Psalm 104:7–9 — waters flee and remain within the boundary God appoints

verses.text: The waters did as he commanded them. They withdrew from the face of the earth into one place outside that expanse, and dry land appeared.
verses.study: Creation responds without resistance. The repeated command-and-fulfillment pattern presents the world as answering its maker faithfully.
crossReferences: Psalm 33:8–9 — what God commands comes into being
Jeremiah 5:22 — God appoints an enduring boundary for the sea

verses.text: On that day he made all the seas according to their gathering places, all the rivers, every gathering of water in the mountains and throughout the earth, all the lakes, all the dew of the earth, seed-bearing plants, everything that sprouts, fruit-bearing trees, forest trees, the garden of Eden in Eden for delight and food, and every plant according to its kind.
verses.study: The third day fills dry land with waters and vegetation. Delight and provision are built into the ordered diversity of creation.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:10–12 — seas, seed-bearing plants, and fruit trees are made by kind
Genesis 2:8–9 — God plants Eden with trees pleasant and good for food

verses.text: God made these four great works on the third day. On the fourth day he made the sun, moon, and stars and placed them in heaven’s expanse to shine upon the whole earth, to rule over day and night, and to divide light from darkness.
verses.study: The heavenly lights serve the earth rather than rule as gods. Their authority is delegated and ordered toward illumination and measured time.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:14–18 — the lights govern day and night and separate light from darkness
Psalm 136:7–9 — the great lights are works of God’s enduring mercy

verses.text: God appointed the sun as a great sign upon the earth for days, Sabbaths, months, festivals, years, weeks of years, jubilees, and all the seasons of the years.
verses.study: The sun marks a layered sacred calendar. Ordinary days and the longest jubilee cycles belong to one divinely ordered structure of time.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:14 — heavenly lights mark signs, appointed times, days, and years
Leviticus 25:8–10 — weeks of years culminate in the jubilee

verses.text: It divides light from darkness and brings well-being so that everything sprouting and growing upon the earth may flourish. He made these three kinds on the fourth day.
verses.study: The light’s ordering work also serves earthly fruitfulness. Cosmic rhythms and living growth are held together within the Creator’s provision.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 33:14 — the sun and months contribute precious produce
Psalm 74:16–17 — God establishes light, sun, seasons, and the earth’s boundaries

verses.text: On the fifth day he made the great sea creatures in the depths of the waters, for these were the first fleshly works made by his hands; he also made fish, everything that moves in the waters, every flying bird, and all their kinds.
verses.study: Animal life begins in sea and sky with abundant kinds. Even the largest creatures of the deep are presented simply as works of God’s hands.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:20–21 — great sea creatures, aquatic life, and birds are created by kind
Psalm 104:25–26 — the vast sea and its great creatures belong to God

verses.text: The sun rose over them for their well-being, and over everything on earth—everything that sprouts from the ground, every fruit-bearing tree, and all flesh.
verses.study: The heavenly light serves the life created beneath it. Plant, animal, and human flourishing all depend on a provision beyond themselves.
crossReferences: Psalm 104:19–23 — the sun orders the rhythms of creatures and human labor
Matthew 5:45 — God makes his sun rise as a gift over the earth

verses.text: He made these three kinds on the fifth day. On the sixth day he made all the animals of the earth, all livestock, and everything that moves upon the earth.
verses.study: Land animals complete another ordered set of living kinds. Their variety remains gathered under a single Creator and a single day.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:24–25 — land animals, livestock, and creeping things are made by kind
Psalm 50:10–11 — every beast and bird belongs to God

verses.text: After all these, he made humanity. Male and female he made them, and he gave them dominion over everything upon the earth and in the seas, over everything that flies, over animals, livestock, everything that moves upon the earth, and over the whole earth. Over all these he gave them dominion.
verses.study: Humanity is created as male and female and receives accountable rule within an already flourishing world. Dominion is a gift from the Creator, not independent ownership.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:26–28 — male and female humanity receives dominion over living creatures
Psalm 8:5–8 — God crowns humanity and places created works under human care

verses.text: He made these four kinds on the sixth day, and all together there were twenty-two kinds.
verses.study: The total count presents creation as complete and ordered. The number will soon be paired with the generations from Adam to Jacob.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:31 — the completed creation is surveyed as very good
1 Corinthians 14:33 — God’s works reflect order rather than confusion

verses.text: He finished all his work on the sixth day: everything in the heavens and on the earth, in the seas and in the abysses, in light and darkness, and in all things.
verses.study: Nothing lies outside the finished work. Every realm named earlier is gathered into the declaration of completion.
crossReferences: Genesis 2:1–2 — heaven, earth, and their host are completed
Nehemiah 9:6 — God made heaven, earth, seas, and everything in them

verses.text: He gave us a great sign, the Sabbath day: we were to work for six days but rest from all work on the seventh day.
verses.study: The speaking angel includes himself among those commanded to rest. The Sabbath becomes a sign observed in the heavenly order before its earthly disclosure.
crossReferences: Exodus 20:9–11 — six days of work are followed by seventh-day rest
Ezekiel 20:12 — Sabbaths are given as a sign of sanctification

verses.text: He commanded all the angels of the presence and all the angels of holiness—these two great kinds—to keep Sabbath with him in heaven and on earth.
verses.study: The highest ministering orders share the Creator’s rest. Sabbath holiness reaches beyond human practice into heavenly worship.
crossReferences: Isaiah 6:2–3 — holy heavenly servants worship before God’s presence
Hebrews 1:6 — God’s angels are commanded in worship

verses.text: He said to us, ‘Look, I will set apart for myself a people from among all peoples. They too will keep the Sabbath day. I will sanctify them for myself as my people and bless them. Just as I sanctified the Sabbath day for myself, so I will sanctify and bless them. They will be my people, and I will be their God.
verses.study: Sanctified time and a sanctified people interpret one another. Israel’s Sabbath is presented as participation in the holiness God established at creation.
crossReferences: Exodus 31:13 — Sabbath is a sign that the Lord sanctifies Israel
Leviticus 20:26 — God separates a people from the nations to be holy

verses.text: I have chosen Jacob’s offspring from among all that I have seen. I have written him down as my firstborn son and sanctified him for myself forever. I will teach them the Sabbath day so that they may rest from all work upon it.’
verses.study: Jacob’s election is described as filial, written, and enduring. Instruction in Sabbath rest is part of learning to live as God’s consecrated firstborn.
crossReferences: Exodus 4:22 — Israel is named God’s firstborn son
Isaiah 44:1–2 — Jacob is chosen and formed as God’s servant

verses.text: Thus he established in it a sign by which they also should keep Sabbath with us on the seventh day: to eat, drink, and bless the one who created all things, just as he blessed and sanctified for himself a treasured people above every people, so that they might keep Sabbath together with us.
verses.study: Sabbath rest is marked by grateful enjoyment and blessing of the Creator. Israel’s earthly observance joins a larger fellowship of holy worship.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 14:2 — Israel is chosen as God’s treasured people
Nehemiah 8:10–12 — holy celebration includes eating, drinking, sharing, and rejoicing

verses.text: He caused his commands to rise before him like a pleasing fragrance acceptable to him through all the days.
verses.study: Obedient commands are pictured as an offering received with delight. Faithful Sabbath practice belongs to worship, not mere inactivity.
crossReferences: Leviticus 1:9 — an obedient offering rises as a pleasing aroma to the Lord
Philippians 4:18 — faithful gifts are described as a fragrant offering acceptable to God

verses.text: There were twenty-two heads of humanity from Adam to Jacob, and twenty-two kinds of work were made up to the seventh day. The latter is blessed and holy, and the former also is blessed and holy; this one together with that one serves for sanctification and blessing.
verses.study: The text pairs the ordered works of creation with the generations leading to Jacob. Both sequences are interpreted through the blessing and holiness of the seventh day.
crossReferences: Genesis 5:1–32 — generations are traced from Adam through the early patriarchs
Genesis 35:9–12 — Jacob receives the ancestral blessing and the name Israel

verses.text: To Jacob and his offspring it was granted that they should always be the blessed and holy ones of the first testimony and law, just as God sanctified and blessed the Sabbath day on the seventh day.
verses.study: Jacob’s descendants are called to embody the holiness announced from creation. Their privilege is inseparable from the testimony and law entrusted to them.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 7:6 — Israel is a holy and chosen people
Romans 9:4 — Israel receives the covenants, law, worship, and promises

verses.text: He made heaven and earth and everything he created in six days, and the Lord made the seventh day holy for all his works. Therefore he commanded concerning it that whoever does any work on it must die, and whoever profanes it must certainly die.
verses.study: The chapter applies creation holiness through the covenant’s most severe legal warning. To profane the day is to reject the sign fixed into creation and entrusted to Israel.
crossReferences: Exodus 31:14–15 — profaning the Sabbath and working on it incur death
Numbers 15:32–36 — deliberate Sabbath violation receives the stated covenant penalty

verses.text: So command the Israelites to observe this day, to keep it holy, to do no work on it, and not to profane it, because it is holier than all other days.
verses.study: Moses must translate heavenly testimony into instruction for Israel. Holiness requires both guarded time and the refusal of ordinary labor.
crossReferences: Exodus 20:8–10 — Israel is commanded to remember and sanctify the Sabbath
Jeremiah 17:21–22 — carrying burdens and work are forbidden on the holy day

verses.text: Whoever profanes it must certainly die, and whoever does any work on it must certainly die forever. Thus the Israelites are to observe this day throughout their generations and not be uprooted from the land, for it is a holy day and a blessed day.
verses.study: Generational observance is connected with continued life in the land. The blessed day demands covenant seriousness rather than casual possession.
crossReferences: Exodus 31:16 — Israel keeps the Sabbath as a covenant throughout generations
Leviticus 26:33–35 — expulsion from the land answers persistent covenant violation

verses.text: Everyone who observes it and rests from all work on it will be holy and blessed through all days, like us.
verses.study: Resting on the seventh day shapes the worshiper beyond that single day. Israel is invited to share the pattern of heavenly holiness and blessing.
crossReferences: Isaiah 56:2 — the one who keeps the Sabbath without profaning it is blessed
Hebrews 4:9–11 — Sabbath rest portrays participation in God’s own rest

verses.text: Declare to the Israelites the law of this day: they must rest upon it and not abandon it through the error of their hearts. They may do no improper work or pursue their own pleasure on it; they may not prepare anything to eat or drink, draw water, or carry through their gates any load that they did not prepare in their dwellings on the sixth day.
verses.study: The command reaches motives, preparation, food, water, and transport. Prior preparation protects the day from being overtaken by ordinary desire and labor.
crossReferences: Exodus 16:22–30 — food is prepared beforehand and gathered on six days
Isaiah 58:13–14 — Sabbath honor turns away from ordinary pleasure and business

verses.text: They must not bring anything in or carry anything out from house to house on that day, because that day is holier and more blessed than any jubilee day of the jubilees. We kept Sabbath on it in heaven before any flesh was taught to keep Sabbath upon it on earth.
verses.study: The prohibition on carrying guards the household expression of rest. Heavenly observance is presented as preceding and authorizing Israel’s earthly practice.
crossReferences: Jeremiah 17:22–27 — no burden is to be carried out of houses or through Jerusalem’s gates
Nehemiah 13:15–19 — gates are shut to prevent Sabbath commerce and burdens

verses.text: The Creator of all blessed it, but he did not sanctify every people and nation to keep Sabbath upon it. Israel alone was sanctified; to them alone he granted eating, drinking, and keeping Sabbath upon it on earth.
verses.study: The day blesses creation broadly while its covenant observance marks Israel particularly. Sabbath enjoyment is portrayed as a granted privilege of consecration.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 5:15 — Israel’s Sabbath command is tied to its rescue from Egypt
Ezekiel 20:12 — Sabbaths are given specifically as a sign between God and Israel

verses.text: The Creator of all blessed this day that he had made for blessing, holiness, and glory above all days.
verses.study: The chapter’s final praise gathers the Sabbath’s qualities: divine blessing, consecrated holiness, and glory surpassing ordinary time.
crossReferences: Genesis 2:3 — God blesses and sanctifies the seventh day
Isaiah 58:13 — the Sabbath is called a delight and the Lord’s holy, honored day

verses.text: This law and testimony was given to the Israelites as an everlasting law throughout their generations.
verses.study: The creation account ends as covenant instruction. What began with the angel’s command to write now stands as testimony intended for every generation.
crossReferences: Exodus 31:16–17 — Israel keeps the Sabbath as an enduring covenant and sign
Deuteronomy 29:29 — revealed things belong to Israel and its children for obedience

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 2 begins the angel’s written account with creation. Each day adds ordered realms and kinds: heavenly ministers and cosmic conditions, the divided waters, dry land and vegetation, the lights that govern time, creatures of sea and sky, land animals, and humanity. The repeated numbering emphasizes completeness, while the angels’ praise shows that the proper response to the created order is worship of its maker.

The chapter gives special attention to sacred time. The sun marks days, festivals, weeks of years, and jubilees, but the seventh day receives a greater role as the sign of God’s finished work. Sabbath is first kept in heaven by the angels of the presence and holiness, then entrusted to Israel as participation in the Creator’s own rest.

Israel and the Sabbath interpret one another in the chapter. God sanctifies the day and sets apart Jacob’s offspring; he blesses the day and blesses his people; the heavenly ministers rest and Israel is invited to rest with them. Eating, drinking, blessing the Creator, and ceasing from labor express a covenant identity rooted in divine election rather than mere inactivity.

The closing commands give that identity practical boundaries. Work, preparation, burdens, carrying, and ordinary pleasure are set aside through preparation on the sixth day. The strict warnings reflect the text’s conviction that holy time belongs to God. The chapter ends where it began—with written law and testimony meant to preserve creation-shaped worship throughout Israel’s generations.

crossReferences: Genesis 1:1–2:3 — creation unfolds across six days and culminates in the blessed seventh day
Exodus 16:22–30 — sixth-day preparation enables Israel to rest on the seventh day
Exodus 20:8–11 — Sabbath observance is grounded in God’s creation and rest
Exodus 31:12–17 — Sabbath is an enduring sign that God sanctifies Israel
Leviticus 23:1–3 — the seventh-day Sabbath stands first among the Lord’s appointed times
Deuteronomy 5:12–15 — Sabbath joins holy rest with Israel’s redemption from slavery
Isaiah 56:1–7 — faithful Sabbath observance is joined to blessing and worship
Isaiah 58:13–14 — honoring the Sabbath brings delight in the Lord
Ezekiel 20:10–20 — Sabbaths function as signs of sanctification amid Israel’s rebellion
Hebrews 4:1–11 — God’s seventh-day rest becomes a pattern for faithful entry into his rest
